title: Senior Product Designer, Toast Support Experiences
tags: R & D : UX : Customer Experience Platform
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

About this role

As a Senior Product Designer for Toast Support Experiences, you will define how restaurants get help across multiple touchpoints: AI-powered chat, voice interactions, human agents, and self-service account management. You'll design the connective tissue between these surfaces, ensuring that a customer's conversation, account context, and support journey feel cohesive, whether they're chatting with Toast IQ, checking their subscription, or being handed off to a support agent.
This role requires thinking in systems. You'll own the interaction language across multiple product surfaces while maintaining a sharp focus: making support effortless for restaurant operators, and making it efficient for the support teams who serve them.
You'll partner closely with product, engineering, and our customer service leadership to define how support works at Toast.

The right ingredients (Requirements)

•
Conversational & voice UX fluency: Shipped conversational interfaces (chat, messaging, or voice) that users trusted and came back to. You understand the mechanics of turn-taking, intent clarification, handoff moments, and when to escalate. 

•
Hands-on systems thinking: Design cohesive experiences across multiple surfaces (web, mobile, voice) and interaction modes (chat, IVR, agent tooling). You see how one flow connects to another and design for the seams, especially handoffs between AI and human support.

•
Pragmatic third-party integration: Experience designing with and around external tools. You can adapt purchased solutions to feel like part of Toast without forcing a square peg into a round hole.

•
Voice AI UX design: Understand conversational flow, context threading, and utterance patterns for voice interactions. You design voice UX (not just visual UI), thinking through IVR trees, prompts, and escalation logic. Deep familiarity with how people actually talk to voice systems.

•
UI/UX rigor: Strong visual design skills demonstrated through a real portfolio. You can prototype interactions, spec components, and push Figma work that sets a high bar. Your work is both functional and thoughtfully crafted.

•
Cross-functional influence: You build conviction within product, engineering, and go-to-market teams. You can make a case for design decisions and get teams aligned behind them.

•
Research-driven approach: You design with data by conducting user research, usability testing, and pull insights from support metrics and customer feedback. You know when to prototype before committing to direction.

•
Familiarity with AI design tooling: You're comfortable working with Claude, V0, Replit, and similar tools.

 

What we'll ask to see

Case studies showing:

•
A conversational or voice experience you designed from scratch or significantly reshaped (not just designed UI for a given flow)

•
How you navigated complexity across multiple surfaces or interaction modes (web + mobile + voice, or chat + voice + human handoff)

•
Evidence of influence: how other teams or designers adopted or built on your approach

•
Research or testing that informed a key design decision

•
Work that felt cohesive despite being built across tools or platforms

 

About you

You bring the same tenets that drive Toast's Design practice:

• Founder's mentality: You own outcomes, not just outputs. You care deeply about whether your designs actually work for support agents and restaurant operators.

• You lift others up: You make the designers around you better through example, feedback, and generosity with your process.

• You drive action through influence: You build trusted relationships across product, engineering, and customer service teams. You can shift a room's perspective without authority.

title: Senior People Systems Analyst
description:

In the coming decades, our world needs far more critical minerals including copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.
KoBold is the leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs-by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.
Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.
KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.
KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

Nice-to-Have

• Familiarity with containerization and orchestration tools (Docker, Azure Kubernetes Service)

• Experience with real-time or low-latency ML systems on Azure (Event Hubs, Stream Analytics)

• Exposure to LLMs or hybrid AI/ML systems, particularly via Azure OpenAI or Microsoft Copilot ecosystem

• Experience building data pipelines with Azure Data Factory, Synapse Pipelines, or Databricks workflows

title: Ronia Raw Photo Collection - United States
description:
Work Location : United States; Remote
We are currently looking for contributors for our Ronia Raw Photo Collection Project.

What is the project about?

We invite photographers, photo hobbyists, visual creators, and anyone passionate about photography to participate in our RAW Photo Collection project.

Do you regularly capture high-quality photos in RAW format to expand your photo library? If the answer is yes, this project allows you to earn extra income by contributing your photos to the development of advanced AI and computer vision technologies. Your images can have a real-world impact beyond your personal library.

Task Description:

Participants may submit both existing photos from their personal archives and newly captured images in RAW format. We’re looking for a wide variety of subjects, styles, lighting conditions, and environments-including nature, events, everyday scenes, objects, and more.

Photos may be captured in RAW and other supported formats using eligible iPhones or digital cameras. Uploading is quick and easy via our mobile app or browser-based data collection tool.

We will be collecting the following types of photos:

• RAW Images : individual, unedited images captured directly from the device.

• Image Pairs: pairs of identical unedited photos, with specific objects present in one and absent in the other photo.

Accepted Formats:
The photos should be native RAW and DNG where applicable (including CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, DNG, RW2, ORF, and PEF). These files retain the raw data captured by the device at the moment the photo was taken.

All submitted photos must be original and taken by you . Photos downloaded from the internet or generated using AI will not be accepted.

Intellectual Property Rights: Participants retain full ownership of all submitted photos, which will be used exclusively for internal purposes by our client and will not be distributed, or published.

Who is eligible?

To participate you should meet the following qualifying criteria:

• Be 18 years or older.

• Be a resident of the United States.

• Be able to upload RAW images or a pair of two images following our instructions.

•
All images should be taken with one of the following devices:

•
iPhone models accepted:

• 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max

• 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max

•
17 Pro, 17 Pro Max

All accepted iPhone models should run iOS 14.3 or later.

No other smartphones are permitted.

•
Digital Cameras

• Full-frame mirrorless

• Full-frame DSLR

• APS-C mirrorless

• APS-C DSL

Where is the project taking place?

This is a fully remote project. You can participate from the comfort of your home or preferred location within the US.

Please note the following location-based limitations:

• Public Images

Public Images are photos taken in publicly accessible places and/or featuring identifiable individuals. We can accept Public Images only if they were captured in the following U.S. states: AL, AK, AZ, AR, FL, GA, HI, ID, KS, LA, ME, MA, MI, MS, MO, NM, NY, NC, ND, OH, OK, PA, SC, SD, VT, WV, WI, WY.

• Non-Public Images

Non-Public Images (for example, photos taken in private settings without public access) are accepted from all U.S. states, except IL, WA, and TX.

Image

How much is the compensation?

You will receive $1.50 USD per each accepted photo. Participants may submit as many photos as they wish across all open categories. Please note that some categories may have submission limits, and once a category is filled, it will be closed. Submissions are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis.

Example earnings:
50 accepted photos x $1,50 = $75 USD

100 accepted photos x $1.50 = $150 USD

Please note that all submissions will be checked by our Quality Assurance team, and compensation will be provided for submitted and accepted photos. The project team will provide you with feedback once the Quality Check process is completed.

As payment methods we offer Wire Transfer, PayPal, Gift Card and Check according to your preference.

title: SoC Engineer

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

- Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

- Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

- Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

- Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

- Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

- Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

- Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

- Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

- Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

- Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

- Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

- Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

- Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

- Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

- Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

- Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

- Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

• Identify and execute tax planning opportunities, including credits, incentives, and entity structuring. Evaluate complex tax legislation changes to mitigate risks and capitalize on opportunities.

• Deep expertise in ASC 740 and SEC tax reporting, including drafting disclosures and working with external auditors.

• Proven ability to develop long-term tax strategy and to review and coach staff, ideally as a player-coach who stays close to technical work.

• Ability to multi-task, establish priorities, and work well with cross-functional teams under pressure.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex tax topics to non-tax executives.

• Proven track record in a dynamic environment, comfortable leading through change.

• Experience leading tax teams within a public SaaS or high-growth technology company.

• Proven track record of managing complex international tax structures and M&A transactions.

Workiva platform experience.

description:
Department: Estimating
Reports to: Chief Estimator / Director of Estimating
Location: Remote
Compensation: Competitive salary based on experience + Performance Bonuses
Enterprise Electrical is looking for a highly skilled Senior Estimator to join our growing team. This position plays a crucial role in shaping our project bidding process and ensuring our competitive edge in the electrical construction sector.
The ideal candidate will possess a strong background in electrical estimation with a minimum of 10 years’ experience in the construction industry, specifically in the commercial and mission critical spaces. You will be responsible for preparing comprehensive cost estimates, analyzing project specifications, and ensuring the accuracy of bid proposals submitted to clients.
Key Responsibilities:

• Accurately prepare detailed cost estimates for electrical construction projects, including labor, materials, and equipment.

• Review and analyze project drawings, specifications, and scope of work.

• Coordinate with project managers, engineers, and design teams to clarify project requirements.

• Develop and maintain relationships with subcontractors and suppliers to obtain accurate pricing.

• Conduct thorough risk analysis and identify areas for cost savings.

• Prepare and submit comprehensive bid proposals to clients.

• Mentor and train junior estimators as needed.

• Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and best practices to enhance the estimating process.

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field

• Minimum of 10 years of experience in electrical estimating within commercial construction.

• Proficient in Estimating Software (e.g., Accubid, PlanSwift, Syspro) and Microsoft Excel.

• Strong understanding of NEC codes and industry standards.

• Exceptional analytical and mathematical skills for accurate cost predictions.

• A proven track record of managing multiple estimates simultaneously and meeting tight deadlines.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with team members and clients.

• Ability to work independently, efficiently, and accurately in a remote or hybrid setting.

• Relevant certifications (e.g., Certified Professional Estimator - CPE) are a plus.

title: Nuuly - Sr DevOps Engineer
description:
Role Summary
Nuuly is searching for a DevOps Engineer to join our growing Platform Engineering team. We are looking for a candidate who will build and maintain features to enhance our systems, as well as serve as a deeply technical guide to our business team as they adopt features built by all engineering teams. Your goal will be to allow for seamless scalability of our production infrastructure and apply your technical expertise to help preclude growth concerns before they occur.
In this role, you will have the opportunity to build a breadth of experience with Kubernetes, Kafka, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). As a DevOps Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining our cloud infrastructure on GCP and managing containerized applications using Kubernetes. The ideal candidate should have more than 3 years of hands-on experience in DevOps practices, with a strong emphasis on GCP services and Kubernetes orchestration, and some experience in asynchronous message brokers (like Kafka & RabbitMQ). You will play a crucial role in optimizing our cloud environment and streamlining our development and deployment processes. This role will impact Nuuly's overall success and growth, driving our scalability, reliability, and efficiency.
Role Responsibilities
A typical week at Nuuly in this role may involve:

• Design, implement, and manage scalable and highly available cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform, including Compute Engine, Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud Networking, and Confluent Kafka.

• Collaborate with software development teams to establish efficient CI/CD pipelines, ensuring smooth and automated application deployments.

• Implement monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions to maintain the health, performance, and security of the cloud infrastructure.

A Phlebotomist serves patients by identifying the best method for retrieving blood; preparing specimens for laboratory testing; and performing screening procedures.  The Phlebotomist will also act as an operations manager for the designated patient service center (PSC) and oversee Natera’s phlebotomy program at the specified location.  Depending upon growth opportunities, this role may also require oversight of other phlebotomists as needed to support patient volume growth. *** IF YOUR STATE REQUIRES A PHLEBOTOMY LICENSE, IT MUST BE SENT IN WITH YOUR RESUME WITH YOUR APPLICATION ***

• Verifies patient by reading patient identification.

• Obtains blood specimens by performing venipunctures and finger sticks.

Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities; reading professional publications; maintaining personal networks; participating in professional organizations.

• Enhances Natera’s phlebotomy reputation by accepting ownership for accomplishing new and different requests; exploring opportunities to add value to job accomplishments.

• Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.

• This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic), in order to perform the job.

• Report any SPI or CAPA or NCR issues to internal Natera product management leadership team Assists with managing all phlebotomy equipment associated with the establishment and running of the patient service center[KC4] , may require heavy lifting of up to 50 pounds of supplies.

• May require reimbursable travel for stocking of supplies May include onboarding, training, and retraining of individual phlebotomists, as deemed necessary to support volume increases.

• Assists with managing Patient Service Center vendors.

• Assists with phlebotomy program management: Monitor distribution and claiming of blood draws Monitor customer feedback Manage small escalations as needed

• Must maintain a current status on Natera’s training requirements.

Evio is a highly unique pharmacy solutions company that was founded by and works closely with health plans to implement transformative (to cost, quality, access and experience) initiatives primarily focused on specialty and other high-cost medication solutions.

In 2020, a group of five amazing Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans that in total serve more than 20 million members recognized that the way medications get to patients needs significant reform-rapidly rising costs and massive system complexities are detrimental to patients and the entire industry. In 2025, Wellmark joined as Evio 's first non-founding investor and sixth owner health plan. Each company made, and continues to make, significant investments to establish Evio as an independent entity to lead this transformation.  

Evio has advanced analytics and contracting capabilities at scale , and a suite of digital tools , to power our high-cost medication solutions. Our solutions act as a self-reinforcing “flywheel” where each element strengthens and feeds into the next, and support an “Only Evio can do that,” mindset and prioritization.

Evio is also a company that has invested heavily in and been highly intentional about people, team and culture. We believe we have created a very special place to work and encourage candidates to observe and ask us about our culture and decide for themselves.

•
Empathy - The people our business serves always come first. We care for our teammates and put ourselves in the shoes of our health plan customers and the patients and clinicians our solutions benefit.

Your technical skills, curiosity, and health plan empathy will drive the evolution of Evio Insights to ensure it continues to meet the needs of health plan customers.

• Explore data to identify signals, trends, utilization patterns, and anomali

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society.

Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our new San Francisco headquarters.

About the Role
Frontier AI companies are increasingly bottlenecked on expert judgment and high-quality data workflows. This team builds the production systems that capture, coordinate, and validate that work at scale - directly between a customer request and the output that ships.
These are long-running, stateful systems. A single job can stay live for days, interleaving automated steps, model inference, and expert review. A step marked "done" can be reopened, re-reviewed, and redone - so "completed" is not always final, state has to tolerate late mutation, and correctness has to survive humans and models disagreeing with each other.
This is a backend systems and orchestration problem: distributed state machines, not pipelines. The architecture is not set. Early engineers will decide what it becomes, and the loop between "I shipped this" and "this mattered" is short.
What You'll Do

- Design services and state models for multi-stage workflows that fan out across automated processing and expert reviewers, then reconcile results into a coherent whole

- Build orchestration primitives - retries, failure recovery, idempotency, auditable state transitions - for jobs that run far longer than a request and can be partially redone after the fact

- Integrate model inference into production workflows without sacrificing debuggability or human oversight

- Build the APIs and tooling that let product, operations, and ML teams operate, debug, and trust these systems at scale

- Own reliability and observability for workflows where a silent failure means a corrupted result, not just a 500
What Makes This Role Different

- You are building the core infrastructure that sits directly between customer requests and the outputs that ship - not internal tooling, not a support system

- This product area is young and strategically central; early engineers are deciding the architecture, not inheriting it

- The inputs are non-deterministic by nature - you are building durable orchestration over humans and models that can disagree with each other on hour 40 of a multi-stage job

description:

GPU deep learning ignited the modern AI era - with NVIDIA hardware and software acting as the foundation for the world’s most ambitious AI, robotics, and autonomous systems workloads. We are growing our teams with the most thoughtful, creative, and driven people on the planet.
NVIDIA is seeking a software engineer with systems software and security experience to join the Data Center Systems Software team. You will investigate and resolve product vulnerabilities and strengthen Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL) practices for platforms including HGX, DGX, and MGX.

What You’ll Be Doing:

• Investigate and reproduce vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and impact, and identify affected products and software versions.

• Assess third-party vulnerabilities and coordinate dependency updates, mitigations, or documented exceptions.

• Drive timely remediation with engineering owners and PSIRT Operations, including risk prioritization, escalation, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.

• Develop or review security fixes, validate mitigations, develop regression tests, and coordinate updates across supported releases.

• Build automation for vulnerability triage, analysis, and tracking.

• Improve SDL practices through threat modeling, security design reviews, and other best-practices.

• Evangelize and drive SDL practices across NVIDIA data center software teams.
What We Need to See:

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• 5+ years of relevant software or security engineering experience.

• Hands-on experience investigating and remediating vulnerabilities, including familiarity with CVSS scoring and CWE classification.

• Experience with secure development practices and security testing tools, such as static analysis, fuzzing, and software composition analysis.

• Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language.

• Experience with modern AI and Agents, including AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of cutting-edge tools and techniques.

• The ability to drive resolution across distributed and diverse engineering teams.

• Solid technical foundation in embedded systems, with the ability to engage credibly in technical discussions around firmware architecture, memory safety, and hardware-software interfaces.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a remote team.

• Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction.
Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

• Product security experience with modern data center systems.

• Knowledge of secure boot, root of trust solutions, attestation, and related technologies such as UEFI, SPDM, or TCG DICE.

• A track record of improving SDL adoption or security automation across engineering teams.

• Demonstrated vulnerability research, security fixes, or open-source security contributions.

title: Senior SecOps Engineer
description:
What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business - where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent - it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior SecOps Engineer to take ownership of security operations at Flagstone. That covers everything from alert triage and incident response through to detection engineering and continuous improvement of how our SOC works.

This is a hands-on role that sits right at the operational end of security. You’ll spend real time in the alert queue, as well as building the detections and automation that make it better. You’ll be right in the middle of complex investigations and P1s, while also shaping how the function operates. You’ll also own our relationship with our managed SOC provider, setting the standards they work to rather than simply receiving their output.

About the team

You’ll sit within Security Engineering, reporting to our Security Team Leader. In this role you’ll own detection, triage and incident response, and act as the technical counterpart to our managed SOC provider. That means directing their scope, holding them to clear detection and response standards, and keeping ownership of anything escalated or high severity in house.

Does this sound like you?

You’re an engineer at heart. You’d rather write the detection than describe it, and you treat detections and automation like any other engineering work: version controlled, tested and documented. You’re the go to expert when something serious happens, and you can explain security risk just as clearly to engineers as to senior stakeholders.

You’re curious about new technology, AI included, and you have a clear view on where it genuinely helps and where it introduces risk.

What you’ll do

You’ll take ownership of our SOC operations and report on their performance and health to stakeholders across the business. You’ll run investigations and incident response for complex or high severity alerts, managing parallel workstreams, keeping stakeholders informed and running post incident reviews through to real changes in detections or process.

You’ll own the detection engineering backlog, building, tuning and retiring detections across Microsoft Sentinel and Defender, mapped to a coverage model such as MITRE ATT&CK. You’ll turn threat intelligence into detection logic and hunting activity, and drive our automation and SOAR maturity by building Logic App playbooks that reduce manual effort without losing judgement on the nuanced cases.

You’ll manage our managed SOC relationship day to day: defining scope and escalation criteria, reviewing performance against SLAs and acting as the technical escalation point for anything they can’t close. You’ll keep playbooks, escalation paths and documentation in shape so the practice scales beyond any one person, and you’ll track metrics like triage time, false positive rate and coverage gaps to drive continuous improvement.

You’ll also explore and introduce AI assisted tooling into SOC workflows, such as triage and enrichment copilots, detectio

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

title: Site Reliability Engineer (London)
description:
ABOUT EDRA

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to join our infrastructure team as the second-in-seat hire. Our team ships fast enough that we're starting to hit GitHub's rate limits, and infrastructure has to stay a month ahead of that. You'll be in key engineering meetings to ensure our infrastructure is ready before anyone asks, and to catch any decisions that may become infrastructure problems later.

This is not a ticket queue. You'll decide what gets built, push back when a managed service already does what someone wants to hand-roll, and invent when no pattern exists. You'll also write real software, not just the infrastructure code underneath it. We run containerized workloads on AWS and GCP, defined in infrastructure as code, with Postgres underneath. Some of our early infrastructure was built quickly before anyone owned it full-time. Part of the job is untangling that while keeping the team moving.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own our cloud infrastructure end to end: provisioning, security, reliability, and the infrastructure as code that defines it.

- Stay ahead of the engineering roadmap and have infrastructure ready before features land, working directly with the founders on where the infrastructure goes next

- Find where developers are waiting and remove the wait, whether that's CI, deployment, or environment spin-up. A person sat waiting is the most expensive thing we run, so rational spend on velocity is always on the table

- Run the reliability practice: monitoring, logging, and alerting that fails loudly with a clear signal, and the response when it does

- Lead large infrastructure builds and own our product security posture

- Make the build-vs-managed-service call, and hold the line when the simpler path is the right one

- Read and write Python well enough to see the infrastructure implications of what the team's building and catch problems before they land

- Own AI model safety and the governance of agentic processes. The team leans on agents for repetitive work, and you make sure nothing unsupervised can act on production infrastructure

- Hand capability to others, and support the team cross-functionally: build the tooling that lets engineers, GTM, the AI team, operations, and compliance do without you what today requires you

- Keep current across cloud and model providers so that when an engineer brings a new announcement, you have a credible answer

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- 5 to 10 years in infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering

- Deep, recent experience running production workloads on AWS or GCP, defined in infrastructure as code. A wide toolkit with one or two areas you go deep on. You won't know every service, and we expect you to learn fast

- Python you've written in anger, in or alongside application code

- Postgres in production, and containerized workloads running under an orchestration platform

- A security instinct: you think about vulnerabilities continuously and patch constantly

- Evidence that you've held down an infrastructure function alone or in a very small team

- Work you can point to where you found an ambiguous problem, designed the fix, and made other people faster as a result

- Comfort saying no to senior people when the infrastructure demands it

RBONUS POINTS

- GCP experience, especially migrations or multi-cloud rollouts

- CloudWatch

The European Payments Initiative is changing that with Wero, a proudly European digital wallet to make payments easier, clearer and more secure. Online, in store, at home and across borders, with your money and data protected under European laws and regulations.

Wero is live in Belgium, France, Germany and the Netherlands and launching very soon in Luxembourg and Austria. Backed by 16 major banks and the two largest European acquirers, we’re building a brand new, proudly European payment system.

🔎 What's in it for you

• Working in a large payment company but looking for a more agile environment where your contributions have visible impact? At EPI, you'll help shape the rules and governance of a brand-new European payment scheme.

At EPI, we embrace a remote-first culture, enabling our teams to work remotely from the country they are based in, with in-person meetings at least once a quarter to foster collaboration and connection.

You’ll work closely with internal stakeholders, member banks and prospective members to ensure the robustness, compliance and evolution of EPI’s scheme framework.

• Collaborate with EPI teams, member banks and stakeholders to ensure the scheme framework evolves alongside business and regulatory needs.

• Manage the onboarding process of new PSP applicants for EPI membership, ensuring completeness, consistency and compliance of submissions.

• Assess applicant documentation from risk, financial stability and AML perspectives, identifying potential concerns and areas requiring clarification.

• Prepare recommendations for the Membership Management Committee, highlighting risks, observations and onboarding decisions.

• Act as a key point of contact for applicant institutions throughout the membership assessment process.

• Ensure accurate management, storage and governance of membership and scheme-related documentation.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance frameworks supporting EPI’s growth and expansion.

• Microsoft PowerPoint

• Confluence

• Microsoft Office 365

• Collaboration and documentation management tools

• Regulatory and governance documentation frameworks

• 5+ years of professional experience in payments, scheme management, regulatory affairs, risk management or a related function.

• A degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Law or a related field is preferred.

• Fluent in English (CEFR C1 or C2); French, German, Dutch or other European languages are a plus.

• Thrive in a remote-first, multicultural environment.

• Strong knowledge of the European payments landscape, including EPC SCT Inst, account-to-account payments, payment regulations and scheme dynamics.

• Proven experience drafting, reviewing or maintaining rules and regulations within a payment scheme or comparable environment.

• Excellent analytical and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex regulatory and business concepts into clear documentation.

• Experience working in a financial institution, payment scheme, fintech or regulated payments organization.

• Knowledge of risk management, financial stability assessments and AML-related controls within payments environments.

title: Basque Speaker Recording Quality Assurance
description:
• Listen carefully to each audio recording and compare it against the corresponding prompt text.

• Identify subtle differences between the spoken audio and written text.

• Correct minor text errors, including missing or added words.

• Identify and correct mispronunciations where applicable.

• Adjust punctuation to accurately reflect pauses, questions, and other aspects of the spoken delivery.

• Apply the appropriate issue tag when the recording contains a significant mismatch or quality problem.

• Distinguish between minor text corrections and issues that require a defined quality tag.

• Follow project guidelines and apply judgment consistently across production units.

• Maintain careful, reliable, and consistent review quality throughout the project.

• Native Basque speaker

• Prior experience with QA, audio review, speech data, transcription, or similar quality-review work is preferred

• Strong attention to detail and ability to identify subtle audio-text mismatches.

• Excellent listening comprehension in the assigned locale.

• Ability to recognize issues such as missing words, added words, mispronunciations, unclear speech, and recording noise.

• Ability to apply defined issue categories accurately and consistently.

• Comfortable making careful judgment calls when reviewing audio recordings.

• Reliable availability for approximately 7 hours per week.

• Work anytime, provided you meet project deadlines and quality standards.

• The work is judgment-heavy, so contributors are expected to prioritize accuracy and consistency rather than simply maximizing speed.

• Tasks and overall workload may shift based on project needs and locale-specific audio volume.

• Consistent availability and high quality are required throughout the assignment.

• Payment is output-based, calculated according to the total number of correctly reviewed utterances.

Our enterprise client, a leading provider of high-quality, diverse datasets for AI model development is seeking skilled native speakers to support a Recording Quality Assurance (RecQA) initiative. In this role, you will listen to existing audio recordings, compare them against the corresponding prompt text, correct minor text-audio mismatches, and identify larger recording or quality issues using defined categories. Your careful review will help ensure high-quality speech data for the client's AI training initiative
Work Assignment and Task Summary (What to Expect)
Contributors will evaluate audio recordings against corresponding prompt text. The role requires carefully listening to each recording to make direct text edits for minor errors (e.g., missing/added words, mispronunciations, or punctuation) and applying specific issue tags (such as Mismatch, Cutoff, Mumble, or Noise) for major discrepancies, ensuring high accuracy and consistent quality across all reviews.

title: Head of Corporate Development
description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken https://kraken.tech/ powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in:

Kraken is growing rapidly across markets, products and geographies. We've already completed five acquisitions, and we're looking for more.

We're seeking an exceptional Head of Corporate Development to identify and execute opportunities that materially accelerate our growth and strategy.

This is not simply an M&A role.

We want someone constantly asking: What could Kraken buy, invest in, partner with or build that would make us stronger, faster or more valuable to our clients?

You'll own our corporate development pipeline, originate opportunities and lead transactions from initial thesis through to execution.

That could mean an acquisition, strategic investment, joint venture, partnership or an entirely different commercial structure.

We care about the strategic outcome, not the transaction structure.

You'll work directly with Kraken's senior leadership and across Product, Engineering, Commercial, Finance and Legal.

🚀 What you’ll own:

Originate opportunities

- Identify companies, technologies and capabilities that could accelerate Kraken's strategy.

- Build relationships with founders, investors and industry leaders.

- Develop investment theses and maintain a global pipeline of opportunities.

- Find interesting opportunities before they become competitive processes.

Evaluate strategic value

- Assess strategic fit, technology, market potential, economics and execution risk.

- Build financial models, valuations and investment cases.

- Present clear recommendations to leadership and the Board.

- Know when to pursue an opportunity - and when to walk away.

Execute transactions

- Lead acquisitions, investments and strategic partnerships end-to-end.

- Own valuation, structuring, due diligence and negotiations.

- Coordinate internal teams and external advisers.

- Navigate complexity and drive transactions to completion.

🧠 What you’ll bring to the party:

We're open-minded about your background. You might come from corporate development, private equity, investment banking, venture capital, strategy or an operating role.You're intellectually curious but practical. You like complexity but don't create it.

You have strong opinions, loosely held. You're comfortable challenging senior leaders and being challenged yourself.

You don't need a large team or elaborate process to get things done.

You can move from analysing a market to calling a founder, building a valuation and negotiating a deal.

What matters is that you bring:

- Exceptional commercial judgement and strategic thinking.

- Strong product and technology understanding.

- Outstanding financial, analytical and valuation skills.

- Experience originating, negotiating and executing complex transactions.

- Confidence engaging directly with founders, CEOs, investors and Boards.

- Intellectual curiosity and the ability to understand unfamiliar businesses quickly.

- Comfort with ambiguity, speed and personal accountability.

- Clear communication and the confidence to challenge conventional thinking.

- Experience in technology, software, energy or utilities - particularly internationally - would be valuable.

Ultimately, we don't measure success by the number of deals completed. We measure it by whether those deals materially change Kraken's trajectory.

That's what we're looking for.

How many companies can say they’ve been in business for over 177 years?!
Here at ZEISS, we certainly can! As the pioneers of science, ZEISS handles the everchanging environments in a fast-paced world, meeting it with cutting edge of technologies and continuous advancements. ZEISS believes that innovation and technology are the key to a sustainable future and solutions for global change. We have a diverse range of portfolios throughout the ZEISS family in segments like, Industrial Quality & Research, Medical Technology, Consumer Markets and Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology. We are a global company with over 42,000 employees and have over 4,000 in the US and Canada alone! Make a difference, come join the team!

In addition to corrective lenses, ZEISS develops the technology used by eye care professionals to test, diagnose, and treat eye conditions. Our deep expertise across optics drives the innovation behind vision care products, including Zeiss eyeglasses.
In this role, you will ensure adherence to healthcare regulations, data privacy laws, and corporate compliance standards, while also providing legal support across other areas such as employment law, franchising business models, commercial contracting, and other legal matters as needed. The ideal candidate is a proactive, business-oriented attorney who can identify regulatory risks, drive compliance strategy, and serve as a trusted legal partner to business leaders in a fast-paced environment.
